title.en: Volume 442 Biographies 229: Xu Shuming, Xue Yunsheng, Zong Shiyanxu, Zi, Hui Zhang, Wang Mingluan, Zhang Lin, Zhou Jiamei, Zhou Derun, Hu Yufen, Zhang Yinhuan
title.raw: 卷442 列傳二百二十九 徐树铭 薛允升 宗室延煦 子 会章 汪鸣銮 长麟 周家楣 周德润 胡燏棻 张荫桓

sentences.zh: 列傳二百二十九

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 229
translations.idiomatic: Biography 229

sentences.zh: 徐樹銘薛允升宗室延煦子會章汪鳴鑾長麟

translations.literal: Xu Shuming, Xue Yunsheng, the Imperial Clansman Yanxu, his son Huizhang, Wang Mingluan, and Chang Lin
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuming · Xue Yunsheng · Imperial Clansman Yanxu · Huizhang · Wang Mingluan · Chang Lin

sentences.zh: 周家楣周德潤胡燏棻張廕桓

translations.literal: Zhou Jiamei, Zhou Derun, Hu Yufen, and Zhang Yinhuang
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jiamei · Zhou Derun · Hu Yufen · Zhang Yinhuang

sentences.zh: 徐樹銘，字壽蘅，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Xu Shuming, style name Shouheng, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shuming, whose style was Shouheng, came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Daoguang 27 (1847), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as a reviser.

sentences.zh: 典四川鄉試。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the Sichuan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Sichuan provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，遷中允，簡山東學政。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he was promoted to junior expositor and was selected as Shandong education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he was promoted to junior expositor and appointed education commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，授兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician and was appointed vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Grand Secretariat academician and received appointment as vice minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 督學福建，按試興、泉。

translations.literal: As education commissioner of Fujian he conducted examinations in Xinghua and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising education in Fujian he conducted examinations in the Xing and Quan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 適莆田、同安呂、黃二氏械鬥，勢洶洶，樹銘喻以大義，手書勸諭文付二氏，躬祭鬥死者而哀之，二氏愧悔；

translations.literal: Just then the Lü and Huang clans of Putian and Tongan were locked in armed feud and the situation was extremely volatile; Shuming reasoned with them on moral grounds, personally wrote exhortations for each clan, went in person to sacrifice to those killed in the fighting and mourned them, and the two clans were filled with shame and repentance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Lü and Huang lineages of Putian and Tongan were engaged in a violent clan fight; Shuming appealed to them on principle, handed each clan a written admonition in his own hand, personally offered sacrifices for the dead and mourned them, and both clans repented.

sentences.zh: 復為立型仁、講讓二塾，訓其子弟，二氏愈益和。

translations.literal: He further established for them the Xingren and Jiangrang academies to instruct their younger members, and the two clans became still more harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded the Xingren and Jiangrang schools to teach their sons and nephews, and the two clans grew increasingly amicable.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，乞歸養。

translations.literal: When his term expired he requested leave to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he asked to go home on leave to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，起署禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Tongzhi reign he was recalled to serve as acting left vice minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 5 (1866) he was recalled to serve as acting left vice minister of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，督學浙江，以薦舉人才中列已罷編修俞樾，嚴旨付吏議，謫遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: The following year, while education commissioner of Zhejiang, he listed among recommended talents the dismissed reviser Yu Yue; a stern edict referred the matter to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation, and he was demoted and transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as Zhejiang education commissioner, he included among recommended talents the dismissed reviser Yu Yue; the throne issued a severe edict for personnel review, and he was demoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，鴻臚寺卿，遭父憂，終喪，起授通政司副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign he was made minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; he mourned his father, completed the mourning period, and was recalled as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he became minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; after his father died he completed mourning and was recalled as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 (1884) he was promoted to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 永定河決，詔樹銘往勘，既至，奏罷河工酌用民力及折價交土章程，民德之。

translations.literal: When the Yongding River burst its banks, the throne ordered Shuming to go and survey the damage; once he arrived he memorialized to abolish certain river works, to employ civilian labor as appropriate, and to institute regulations for delivering earth at a fixed price, and the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongding River broke its banks, the court sent Shuming to inspect; on arrival he memorialized to suspend certain works, use civilian labor judiciously, and adopt rules for commuted earth deliveries at set prices, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 法越事急，念海道梗阻，乃疏請漕糧改歸河運，敕直隸總督治南運全河。

translations.literal: As the Franco-Vietnamese crisis grew urgent, mindful that the sea route was obstructed, he memorialized that grain transport should revert to the canal route, and the throne ordered the governor-general of Zhili to repair the entire Southern Transport Canal.
translations.idiomatic: With the Sino-French crisis pressing and the sea lanes blocked, he memorialized to shift tribute grain back to canal transport, and the throne ordered the Zhili governor-general to restore the full Southern Transport Canal.

sentences.zh: 十二年，補左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12 (1886) he was appointed left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時議廢當十錢，復制錢，民心惶惑。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of abolishing the ten-cash coins and restoring standard cash, and popular sentiment was alarmed and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time policy debated abolishing the ten-cash coins and restoring standard copper cash, and public anxiety ran high.

sentences.zh: 樹銘言於戶部尚書閻敬銘，請發倉廩，俾民以當十錢購粟，糶平而錢不廢，民乃安。

translations.literal: Shuming spoke to Minister of Revenue Yan Jingming, asking that granaries be opened so the people could use ten-cash coins to buy grain; grain was sold at fair prices while the coins were not abolished, and the people were thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming urged Minister of Revenue Yan Jingming to release grain from the state granaries so people could exchange ten-cash coins for grain at fair prices without abolishing the coins, and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 15 (1889) he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷充順天、浙江鄉試正副考官，會試總裁。

translations.literal: He served in succession as chief and associate examiner for the Shuntian and Zhejiang provincial examinations and as chief examiner for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as chief and associate examiner for the Shuntian and Zhejiang provincial examinations and as metropolitan examination director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中東構釁，樹銘數上封事，皆不報。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as conflict arose in the Middle East, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which received a response.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 (1894), when war broke out in the Middle East, Shuming submitted several sealed memorials, none of which was answered.

sentences.zh: 旋遷左都御史，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to left censor-in-chief and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to left censor-in-chief and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 疏請行蠶政，敕督撫令有司營辦，以從違為舉劾，上嘉納，下其疏各省。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the promotion of sericulture; the throne ordered governors and governors-general to have local officials undertake the work, with compliance or defiance made grounds for commendation or impeachment; the emperor approved and circulated his memorial to all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to revive sericulture; the throne ordered governors to have local officials organize it, with obedience or neglect as grounds for reward or impeachment; the emperor approved and sent his memorial to every province.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 25 (1899) he was appointed minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 旋病卒，予優恤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness and was granted generous posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died, and was granted generous posthumous favors.

sentences.zh: 樹銘幼穎異，問學於何桂珍、曾國籓、倭仁、唐鑑諸人。

translations.literal: Shuming was precocious as a child and studied under He Guizhen, Zeng Guofan, Woren, Tang Jian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shuming was exceptionally bright and studied under He Guizhen, Zeng Guofan, Woren, Tang Jian, and others.

sentences.zh: 生平無私蓄，惟嗜鐘鼎書畫，藏書數十萬卷，雖耄猶勤學不倦雲。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he amassed no private wealth; he delighted only in bronzes, calligraphy, and painting, and kept several hundred thousand volumes in his library; even in old age he studied tirelessly, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He accumulated no private fortune in his lifetime, cared only for bronzes, calligraphy, and painting, and owned several hundred thousand books; even in old age he is said never to have wearied of study.

sentences.zh: 薛允升，字云階，陝西長安人。

translations.literal: Xue Yunsheng, style name Yunjie, was a native of Chang'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yunsheng, whose style was Yunjie, came from Chang'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a clerk of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Xianfeng 6 (1856) and was appointed a clerk of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，出知江西饒州府。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to director and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，授四川成綿龍茂道，調署建昌。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Guangxu reign he was appointed intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan and was transferred to act as prefect of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 (1877) he was appointed intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan and transferred to act as prefect of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷山西按察使。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 值大祲，治賑，綜覈出入，民獲甦。

translations.literal: A great famine occurred during his tenure; he directed relief efforts, audited receipts and disbursements comprehensively, and the people were able to recover.
translations.idiomatic: A severe famine struck during his tenure; he organized relief, audited all receipts and expenditures, and the people were able to recover.

sentences.zh: 又明年，晉山東布政使，權漕運總督。

translations.literal: The year after that he was promoted to financial commissioner of Shandong and acted as grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to financial commissioner of Shandong and acted as grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮上患劇盜久未獲，允升诇得其巢，遣吏士往捕。

translations.literal: On the Huai a notorious band of robbers had long gone uncaptured; Yunsheng spied out their lair and dispatched officials and constables to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: A vicious gang on the Huai had long evaded capture; Yunsheng located their hideout and sent officers to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 歲除夕，盜方飲酒，未戒備，悉就執。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve the robbers were drinking and off their guard; all were taken at once.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve the bandits were feasting and unprepared; every one of them was seized.

sentences.zh: 六年，召為刑部侍郎，歷禮、兵、工三部，而佐兵部為久。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as vice minister of the Board of Punishments, served in succession in the Boards of Rites, War, and Works, and assisted the Board of War for the longest period.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 (1880) he was summoned as vice minister of the Board of Punishments, served in turn in the Boards of Rites, War, and Works, and assisted the Board of War the longest.

sentences.zh: 念國家養兵勇糜餉糈，因條列練兵裁勇機宜，上嘉納。

translations.literal: Mindful that the state maintained troops and braves at vast expense in provisions and pay, he set forth in detail the measures appropriate for drilling troops and reducing braves; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that the state spent heavily feeding troops and braves, he laid out measures for training regulars and cutting irregular forces, which the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 19 (1893) he was appointed minister of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 初，允升觀政刑曹，以刑名關民命，窮年討測律例，遇滯義筆諸冊，久之有所得。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yunsheng began service in the penal offices, he held that criminal nomenclature bore on the people's lives; year after year he studied and tested the statutes, and whenever he encountered a doubtful point he wrote it in his notebooks until in time he gained mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career Yunsheng served in the penal offices; because legal labels touched the lives of the people, he spent years probing the statutes and noting every doubtful point in his notebooks until he had mastered them.

sentences.zh: 或以律書求解，輒為開導，而其為用壹歸廉平。

translations.literal: When others sought explanations from his legal writings he would instruct them, yet in application he always returned to fairness and impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: When others asked him to explain the codes he would guide them, yet in practice he always aimed at fairness.

sentences.zh: 凡所定讞，案法隨科，人莫能增損一字。

translations.literal: Every judgment he rendered followed the statute to the letter, and no one could add or subtract a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Every verdict he fixed matched the statute article for article, and no one could alter a single character.

sentences.zh: 長官信仗之，有大獄輒以相囑。

translations.literal: His superiors trusted and relied on him; whenever a major case arose they would entrust it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors trusted him completely; major cases were routinely assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 其鞫囚如與家人語，務使隱情畢達，枉則為之平反。

translations.literal: When he interrogated prisoners he spoke as though to family members, striving to bring hidden facts fully to light, and if there was injustice he would set it right.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned prisoners as gently as if speaking to kin, determined to bring every hidden fact to light, and reversed verdicts when he found injustice.

sentences.zh: 始以治王宏罄獄顯名。

translations.literal: He first won renown through his handling of the Wang Hongqing case.
translations.idiomatic: He first became famous for resolving the Wang Hongqing case.

sentences.zh: 蓋民有墮水死者，團防局勇已不勝榜掠，承矣；

translations.literal: A commoner had drowned; the braves of the local defense corps had already beaten a confession out of someone beyond endurance, and the case had been accepted as closed.
translations.idiomatic: The case concerned a commoner who had drowned; local defense braves had tortured a confession out of someone, and the matter was treated as settled.

sentences.zh: 允升覆訊，事白。

translations.literal: Yunsheng re-examined the case and the truth came to light.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng re-examined the case and the truth emerged.

sentences.zh: 厥後江寧民周五殺硃彪，遁；

translations.literal: Later a Jiangning commoner named Zhou Wu killed Zhu Biao and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Jiangning commoner named Zhou Wu killed Zhu Biao and fled.

sentences.zh: 參將胡金傳欲邀功，捕僧紹棕、曲學如論死。

translations.literal: The deputy commander Hu Jinzhuan wished to claim merit and arrested the monks Shaozong and Qu Xueru and had them sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Hu Jinzhuan, eager for credit, arrested the monks Shaozong and Qu Xueru and sought the death penalty for them.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士陳寶琛糾彈之，上命允升往按，廉得實，承審官皆懲辦如律。

translations.literal: The reader-in-waiting Chen Baochen impeached him; the emperor ordered Yunsheng to investigate on the spot, and when the facts were verified all the trial officials were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Chen Baochen impeached him; the emperor sent Yunsheng to investigate, established the facts, and all trial officials were punished as the law required.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，太監李萇材、張受山構眾擊殺捕者，嚴旨付部議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the eunuchs Li Changcai and Zhang Shoushan gathered a mob and killed those sent to arrest them; a stern edict referred the matter to the Board for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 22 (1896) the eunuchs Li Changcai and Zhang Shoushan rallied a crowd and killed the arresting officers; a stern edict ordered the Board of Punishments to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 允升擬援光棍例治之，而總管太監李蓮英為乞恩，太后以例有「傷人致死、按律問擬」一語，敕再議。

translations.literal: Yunsheng proposed applying the statute on idle ruffians, but Chief Eunuch Li Lianying pleaded for mercy; the Empress Dowager cited the phrase in the statute "if injury results in death, sentence according to law," and ordered reconsideration.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng proposed applying the statute on idle ruffians, but Chief Eunuch Li Lianying begged clemency; the Empress Dowager cited the phrase "where injury causes death, sentence according to law" and ordered reconsideration.

sentences.zh: 允升言：「李萇材等一案，既非謀故鬥殺，不得援此語為符合。

translations.literal: Yunsheng said: "In the case of Li Changcai and others, since this was neither premeditated murder nor fighting resulting in death, that phrase cannot be invoked as a match.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng replied: "The case of Li Changcai and the others is neither premeditated murder nor brawling that ends in death, so that phrase cannot apply.

sentences.zh: 且我朝家法嚴，宦寺倍治罪。

translations.literal: Moreover, our dynasty's household law is strict, and eunuchs are punished at double the ordinary rate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our dynasty's domestic law is severe, and palace eunuchs are punished at double the ordinary rate.

sentences.zh: 此次從嚴懲治，不能仰體哀矜之意，已愧於心；

translations.literal: To punish them severely this time already fails to embody the intent of compassionate forbearance, and I am already troubled in conscience.
translations.idiomatic: Even this strict punishment cannot fully embody compassionate mercy, and I already feel uneasy in conscience.

sentences.zh: 倘复遷就定讞，並置初奉諭旨於不顧，則負疚益深。

translations.literal: If we now bend the verdict again and set aside the initial imperial instruction entirely, my burden of guilt will be still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: If we bend the verdict further and disregard the original imperial instruction, my guilt will be all the deeper.

sentences.zh: 夫立法本以懲惡，而法外亦可施仁。

translations.literal: Legislation exists fundamentally to punish evil, yet beyond the law mercy may also be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Law exists to punish evil, yet mercy may be shown outside the strict letter.

sentences.zh: 皇上果欲肅清輦轂，裁仰閹宦，則仍依原奏辦理。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to purify the capital and restrain palace eunuchs, then the original memorial should still be followed.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to cleanse the capital and curb palace eunuchs, then the original memorial should stand.

sentences.zh: 若以為過嚴，或誅首而宥從，自在皇上權衡至當，非臣等所敢定擬也。

translations.literal: If it is thought too severe, to execute the ringleaders and spare the followers rests entirely with Your Majesty's balanced judgment; it is not for us ministers to presume to fix the sentence.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty deems it too harsh, to execute the leaders and spare the followers is entirely within Your Majesty's judgment; we ministers dare not fix the sentence ourselves.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，仍敕部議罪。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the throne still ordered the Board to deliberate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial went up, the throne still ordered the Board to deliberate punishment.

sentences.zh: 其時蓮英遍囑要人求末減，允升不為動。

translations.literal: At that time Lianying importuned influential men everywhere to seek mitigation, but Yunsheng was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lianying pressed influential men everywhere to seek leniency, but Yunsheng would not budge.

sentences.zh: 復奏請處斬張受山，至李萇材傷人未死，量減為斬監候，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized again requesting execution of Zhang Shoushan; as for Li Changcai, since his victims were injured but not killed, the sentence was reduced to beheading with imprisonment awaiting review, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to execute Zhang Shoushan; for Li Changcai, since his victims were wounded but not killed, the sentence was reduced to beheading with imprisonment awaiting review, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，其從子濟關說通賄，御史張仲炘、給事中蔣式芬先後論劾，允升坐不遠嫌，鐫三級，貶授宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his nephew Ji was implicated in bribery through influence; the censor Zhang Zhongxin and the supervising secretary Jiang Shifen impeached him in succession; Yunsheng was punished for failing to keep his distance, was demoted three ranks, and was appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 23 (1897) his nephew Ji was implicated in bribery through influence; Censor Zhang Zhongxin and Supervising Secretary Jiang Shifen impeached him in turn; Yunsheng was faulted for not keeping his distance, demoted three ranks, and appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 次年，謝病歸。

translations.literal: The following year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳禍作，兩宮幸西安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disaster erupted and the two palaces took refuge in Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 (1900) the Boxer disaster broke out and the two palaces fled to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 允升赴行在，復起用刑部侍郎，尋授尚書。

translations.literal: Yunsheng went to the traveling court, was reappointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments, and soon received appointment as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng went to the traveling court, was reappointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments, and soon minister.

sentences.zh: 以老辭，不允。

translations.literal: He pleaded old age and declined, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and declined, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，回鑾，從駕至河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the court returned to the capital, he accompanied the imperial procession as far as Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 27 (1901), when the court returned to the capital, he accompanied the procession as far as Henan.

sentences.zh: 病卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: He died of illness; posthumous favors followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness; posthumous favors followed statute.

sentences.zh: 箸有漢律輯存六卷、漢律決事比四卷、唐明律合編四十卷、服制備考四卷、讀例存疑五十四卷。

translations.literal: His published works include six juan of Collected Han Statutes, four juan of Han Statutory Precedents, forty juan of the Tang and Ming Codes Combined, four juan of Mourning Regulations with Notes, and fifty-four juan of Doubts on Reading Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Collected Han Statutes in six juan, Han Statutory Precedents in four juan, the Tang and Ming Codes Combined in forty juan, Mourning Regulations with Notes in four juan, and Doubts on Reading Precedents in fifty-four juan.

sentences.zh: 子浚，光緒六年進士，官禮部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Jun passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Guangxu reign and served as director in the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun took his jinshi in Guangxu 6 and served as director in the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宗室延煦，字樹南，隸正藍旗，直隸總督慶祺子。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clansman Yanxu, style name Shunan, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner and was the son of Qingqi, governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Clansman Yanxu, style Shunan, of the Plain Blue Banner, was son of Qingqi, governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以任子官禮部主事。

translations.literal: Through the privilege of hereditary office he was appointed a clerk of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Board of Rites as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕北狩，錄城防功，擢四品京堂。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the imperial carriage went north on campaign, his service in defending the capital was recorded and he was promoted to a fourth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 13 (1863), when the court fled north, his merit in defending the capital was recorded and he was promoted to a fourth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 明年，授贊善。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed tutor.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，除盛京兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician and was appointed vice minister of the Board of War at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretariat academician and was appointed vice minister of the Board of War at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，調戶部，數勘辦展邊墾地。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Tongzhi reign he was transferred to the Board of Revenue and repeatedly investigated and handled the opening of frontier wasteland for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6 (1867) he was transferred to the Board of Revenue and repeatedly investigated frontier land reclamation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，移督倉場。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to supervise the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 11 (1872) he was transferred to supervise the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 與漢侍郎畢道遠疏請漕糧起運本色濟兵食，議行。

translations.literal: Together with the Han vice minister Bi Daoyuan he memorialized that tribute grain should be shipped in kind to supply military rations, and this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: With Han vice minister Bi Daoyuan he memorialized that tribute grain should move in kind to feed the troops, and the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，出為熱河都統，以圍場曠莽，易叢姦宄，請增置營汛資守禦。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he was sent out as commander-in-chief of Rehe; because the hunting grounds were vast and wild and easily harbored criminals, he requested additional garrison posts and funds for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 (1876) he was sent out as commander-in-chief of Rehe; the hunting grounds were vast and lawless, so he asked for more garrison posts and funds to guard them.

sentences.zh: 有土寇王致岡者，構眾擾平泉、赤峰、建昌諸處，積為民患，官軍莫能捕，至是遣守備松恩剿平之。

translations.literal: There was a local bandit named Wang Zhigang who gathered a mob and harassed Pingquan, Chifeng, Jianchang, and other places, long a scourge on the people whom government troops could not capture; at this time he sent Assistant Commander Song En to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: A local bandit, Wang Zhigang, had long led a gang harassing Pingquan, Chifeng, Jianchang, and elsewhere beyond the reach of government troops; Yanxu now sent Assistant Commander Song En to wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 尋移疾​​去。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he resigned on grounds of illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 九年，授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 (1883) he was appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 念會典事例自嘉慶間續修，中更六十餘年，典章制度，視昔彌劇。

translations.literal: He reflected that the Collected Statutes and precedents had been continued in revision since the Jiaqing reign, and in the more than sixty years since, statutes and institutions had become far more complex than before.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that the Collected Statutes had last been revised under Jiaqing, and in the sixty-odd years since, institutions had grown far more complex.

sentences.zh: 及今不修，恐文獻無徵，難免舛漏。

translations.literal: If they were not revised now, he feared the documentary record would lack authority and errors would be hard to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: If revision waited longer, he feared the documentary record would lack support and errors would multiply.

sentences.zh: 疏請敕廷臣集議開館，限年修明憲典，得旨報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that the court order ministers to meet and discuss opening a compilation office, with a time limit for completing the statutes; the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a court conference to open a compilation office with a deadline to revise the statutes; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉理籓院尚書，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 he was promoted to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 萬壽聖節，大學士左宗棠未隨班叩祝，延煦上疏論劾。

translations.literal: On the imperial birthday the Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang did not follow the ranks in offering congratulations; Yanxu memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial birthday Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang failed to join the congratulatory ranks; Yanxu memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 略謂：「左宗棠職居首列，鴻臚引班時，竟步出乾清門，不勝駴詫！

translations.literal: He wrote in summary: "Zuo Zongtang holds the foremost rank; when the Court of State Ceremonial led the ranks in salutation, he actually walked out through the Qianqing Gate—I was beyond astonishment!
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in part: "Zuo Zongtang stands at the head of the civil roster; when the Court of State Ceremonial led the ranks in salutation, he actually walked out through the Qianqing Gate—nothing could astonish me more!

sentences.zh: 國家優禮大臣，宗棠被恩尤重。

translations.literal: The state treats great ministers with exceptional favor, and Zongtang has received grace beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The state honors great ministers generously, and Zongtang has received extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 縱捐頂踵，未報萬一，乃躬履尊嚴之地，絕無誠敬之心。

translations.literal: Even were he to give his head and heels, he could not repay one ten-thousandth of it; yet he personally trod this most solemn ground with not the slightest sincere reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Though he offered head and heels he could not repay a fraction of it; yet he entered this most solemn precinct without the least sincere reverence.

sentences.zh: 如曰遘疾，曷弗請假？

translations.literal: If he claims illness, why did he not request leave?
translations.idiomatic: If he was ill, why did he not ask for leave?

sentences.zh: 而必故亂班聯，害禮負恩，莫或斯等！

translations.literal: Yet he deliberately disrupted the ranks, harmed ritual, and betrayed grace—none can equal this!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he willfully broke the ranks, injured ritual, and betrayed imperial grace—who equals this?

sentences.zh: 」疏上，下宗棠吏議，以延煦語過當，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, Zuo Zongtang was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation; because Yanxu's language was excessive, an edict stripped his office but retained him in post.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial went up, Zuo was referred to personnel review; because Yanxu's language was excessive, an edict stripped his rank but kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 會山東民埝決口，言者劾巡撫陳士傑誤工狀，命延煦偕祁世長往按，白其誣而言其失計。

translations.literal: At that time a Shandong dyke burst; critics impeached Governor Chen Shijie for misreporting the works; the throne ordered Yanxu together with Qi Shichang to investigate on the spot, and they cleared him of false accusation while stating where his planning had failed.
translations.idiomatic: When a Shandong dyke burst, critics impeached Governor Chen Shijie for misreporting the works; Yanxu and Qi Shichang were sent to investigate, cleared him of false charges, but noted where his planning had failed.

sentences.zh: 又以遵旨巡察海防，具圖說以上，謂：「煙台、旅順對峙，海面至此一束，兩岸同心扼守要隘，津、沽得有鎖鑰。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to inspect coastal defenses as instructed and submitted illustrated reports, stating: "Yantai and Lüshun face each other; the sea narrows to a single channel here—if both shores coordinate in holding the critical passes, Tianjin and the mouth of the Hai will have a lock and key.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect coastal defenses, he submitted illustrated reports stating: "Yantai and Lüshun face each other where the sea narrows to a single channel; if both shores hold the passes together, Tianjin and the Hai mouth will have their lock and key.

sentences.zh: 防守之法，應如何測淺深，審沙線，備船砲，設水師；

translations.literal: As to methods of defense, how to sound shallows and depths, examine sandbars, prepare ships and cannon, and establish a naval force;
translations.idiomatic: For defense one must sound depths, chart sandbars, ready ships and guns, and establish a navy;

sentences.zh: 募諳海戰之人，必有制勝之策。

translations.literal: Recruit men skilled in naval warfare, and there will surely be a strategy for victory.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit men versed in sea combat, and a winning strategy will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 」上韙其議，特宣示。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his proposal and issued a special proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his proposal and issued a special proclamation.

sentences.zh: 還京，再移疾，不允。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again requested leave on grounds of illness, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he again asked sick leave, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兩宮祇謁東陵，詣孝貞顯皇后陵寢，慈禧皇太后不欲行拜跪禮，延煦持不可，面諍數四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the two palaces went to pay respects at the Eastern Tombs and visited the mausoleum of Empress Xiaozhenxian; the Empress Dowager Cixi did not wish to perform the bowing and kneeling rites, and Yanxu held this unacceptable, arguing face to face several times.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12 the two palaces visited the Eastern Tombs and the tomb of Empress Xiaozhenxian; Empress Dowager Cixi refused the bowing and kneeling rites, and Yanxu objected repeatedly in face-to-face argument.

sentences.zh: 方是時，太后怒甚，禮部長官咸失色，延煦從容無少變。

translations.literal: At that moment the Empress Dowager was extremely angry and the chiefs of the Board of Rites all turned pale, yet Yanxu remained composed without the slightest change.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was furious and the Board of Rites chiefs turned pale, but Yanxu remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 太后卒無以難，不得已跪拜如儀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ultimately had no grounds to object and was obliged to bow and kneel according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refute him, the Empress Dowager at last performed the bowing and kneeling rites as required.

sentences.zh: 延煦起家貴介，以文詞受主知，而立朝大節侃侃無所撓，士論偉之。

translations.literal: Yanxu came from a noble house and won the ruler's favor through literary talent, yet in great matters of state he stood firm and unbending; public opinion admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Born to noble rank and favored for his literary gifts, Yanxu nonetheless stood unshaken on great matters of state, and scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 子會章，光緒二年進士，歷官理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Huizhang passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Guangxu reign and served in succession as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huizhang took his jinshi in Guangxu 2 and rose to vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊戌政變，漢京朝官罹法網者眾。

translations.literal: During the Wuxu coup many Han officials at the capital fell under the law.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuxu coup many Han capital officials were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 會章獨奏論刑獄貴持其平，不當以滿、漢分畛域，言人所不敢言，論者謂其伉直有父風。

translations.literal: Huizhang alone memorialized that in criminal cases fairness must be upheld and that Manchu and Han should not be divided by boundary; he spoke what others dared not speak, and critics said his forthrightness matched his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhang alone memorialized that criminal justice must remain even-handed and that Manchu and Han must not be treated as separate realms; he said what others dared not say, and critics called his bluntness his father's legacy.

sentences.zh: 汪鳴鑾，字柳門，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Mingluan, style name Liumen, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mingluan, style Liumen, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少劬學。

translations.literal: As a youth he studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: He was a diligent student from youth.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Tongzhi reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷司業，益覃研經學，謂：「聖道垂諸六經，經學非訓詁不明，訓詁非文字不著。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of studies and devoted himself further to classical learning, saying: "The sage's Way is embodied in the Six Classics; classical learning cannot be clear without exegesis, and exegesis cannot be established without written characters.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of studies, he deepened his study of the classics, saying: "The sage's Way rests in the Six Classics; exegesis alone clarifies classical learning, and characters alone make exegesis clear.

sentences.zh: 」治經當從許書入手，嘗疏請以許慎從祀文廟。

translations.literal: " To study the classics one should begin with Xu Shen's dictionary; he once memorialized requesting that Xu Shen be admitted to sacrifices in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: " Classical study should begin with Xu Shen; he once memorialized to have Xu Shen enshrined in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 歷督陝甘、江西、山東、廣東學政，典河南、江西、山東鄉試，顓重實學，號得士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as education commissioner of Shaanxi-Gansu, Jiangxi, Shandong, and Guangdong, presided over the Henan, Jiangxi, and Shandong provincial examinations, stressed practical learning, and was renowned for selecting talent.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised education in Shaanxi-Gansu, Jiangxi, Shandong, and Guangdong, presided over provincial examinations in Henan, Jiangxi, and Shandong, favored practical learning, and was known for finding good men.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，父憂歸，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Guangxu reign he returned home to mourn his father; when mourning ended he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 he went home for his father's mourning; after mourning he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 歷遷內閣學士，晉工部侍郎，兼筦戶部三庫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician and to vice minister of the Board of Works, and concurrently managed the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of the Board of Works, and concurrently managed the Board of Revenue's three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 十六年，赴吉林按事，與尚書敬信俱。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went to Jilin to investigate a matter, together with Minister Jingxin.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 16 he went to Jilin on an investigation with Minister Jingxin.

sentences.zh: 二十年，主禮部試。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he directed the metropolitan examination for the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he directed the metropolitan examination for the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時日韓釁起，朝議紛呶。

translations.literal: At that time conflict with Japan had arisen and court debate was clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: War with Japan had broken out and court debate grew heated.

sentences.zh: 詔行走總理各國事務衙門，充五城團防大臣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to serve in the Zongli Yamen and appointed him commander of the Five-City Defense Corps.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen and appointed commander of the Five-City Defense Corps.

sentences.zh: 調吏部右侍郎，兼貳刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Civil Office and concurrently assisted the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Civil Office and concurrently assisted the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 逾年，和議成，日人堅索台灣，鳴鑾力陳不可，稱上意。

translations.literal: The following year peace was made, but the Japanese firmly demanded Taiwan; Mingluan strongly argued this was unacceptable and won the emperor's approval.
translations.idiomatic: The next year peace was signed, but Japan insisted on taking Taiwan; Mingluan argued forcefully against it and matched the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 時上久親政，數召見朝臣，鳴鑾奏對尤切直。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had long taken personal rule and frequently summoned courtiers; Mingluan's answers were especially blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long ruled in person and often summoned ministers; Mingluan's replies were especially blunt.

sentences.zh: 忌者達之太后，故抑揚其語，太后信之，上不自安。

translations.literal: Enemies reported this to the Empress Dowager and deliberately twisted his tone of voice; the Empress Dowager believed them, and the emperor grew uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies carried word to the Empress Dowager and distorted his tone in audience; she believed them, and the emperor grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 其冬，遂下詔曰：「朕侍奉皇太后，仰蒙慈訓，大而軍國機宜，小而起居服禦，體恤朕躬，無微不至。

translations.literal: That winter an edict was issued stating: "I attend upon the Empress Dowager and receive her gracious instruction; in great matters of military and state policy and in small matters of daily life and dress, she cares for my person with boundless thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict ran: "I serve the Empress Dowager and receive her gracious instruction; in great affairs of state and small matters of daily life she cares for me without limit.

sentences.zh: 乃有不學無術之徒，妄事揣摩，輒於召對時語氣抑揚，罔知輕重。

translations.literal: Yet there are unlearned and incompetent men who recklessly speculate and, whenever summoned to audience, raise and lower their tone without knowing what is weighty or light.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unlearned men recklessly speculate and, at imperial audiences, modulate their tone without knowing weight from lightness.

sentences.zh: 如侍郎汪鳴鑾、長麟，上年屢次召見，信口妄言，跡近離間。

translations.literal: Such as Vice Minister Wang Mingluan and Chang Lin, who were repeatedly summoned last year and spoke rashly, their conduct bordering on sowing division.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Mingluan and Chang Lin, repeatedly summoned last year, spoke rashly in ways bordering on division.

sentences.zh: 本欲即行治罪，因軍務方棘，隱忍未發。

translations.literal: I originally intended to punish them at once, but because military affairs were pressing I restrained myself and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to punish them immediately, but with military affairs pressing I held back.

sentences.zh: 今特曉諭諸臣，知所儆惕。

translations.literal: Now I specially instruct all ministers to know caution and vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Now I warn all ministers to take heed.

sentences.zh: 汪鳴鑾、長麟並革職，永不敘用。

translations.literal: Wang Mingluan and Chang Lin were both dismissed from office and permanently barred from appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mingluan and Chang Lin were dismissed and permanently barred from office.

sentences.zh: 嗣後內外大小臣工有敢巧言嘗試者，朕必治以重罪。

translations.literal: Hereafter any official inside or outside the court who dares to test me with clever words, I shall punish with severe penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Any official who dares such clever speech hereafter will be punished severely.

sentences.zh: 」既罷歸，主講杭州詁經精舍、敷文書院。

translations.literal: " After dismissal he returned home and lectured at the Gijing Jingshe Academy and the Fuwen Academy in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Dismissed, he lectured at the Gijing Jingshe and Fuwen academies in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangxu 32.

sentences.zh: 長麟，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Chang Lin was a man of the Bordered Blue Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Lin was of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年繙譯進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the translation metropolitan examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 he passed the translation metropolitan examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 累至戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to vice minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 周家楣，字小棠，江蘇宜興人。

translations.literal: Zhou Jiamei, style name Xiaotang, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jiamei, style Xiaotang, came from Yixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the metropolitan examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Xianfeng 9 and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，改禮部主事，充總理各國事務衙門章京。

translations.literal: After leaving the Hanlin academy he was transferred to a clerk of the Board of Rites and served as a secretary in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Hanlin, he became a Board of Rites clerk and a Zongli Yamen secretary.

sentences.zh: 其時教禍棘，四川總督駱秉章夙持正，外人以將軍崇實易與，遇事輒就決之，數興大獄，至殺平民二百人，勿之問。

translations.literal: At that time missionary troubles were acute; Governor-General Luo Bingzhang of Sichuan had long been upright, but foreigners regarded General Chongshi as easier to deal with and constantly sought decisions from him, repeatedly opening major cases and even killing two hundred civilians without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Missionary troubles were acute; Sichuan Governor-General Luo Bingzhang was upright, but foreigners found General Chongshi pliable and repeatedly sought his rulings, opening major cases and killing two hundred civilians without consequence.

sentences.zh: 家楣上書執政，極言其害，請教案歸總督裁決，卒如所言。

translations.literal: Jiamei wrote to those in power, strongly stating the harm and requesting that missionary cases be decided by the governor-general; in the end matters proceeded as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamei wrote to the leadership, denounced the harm, and asked that missionary cases return to the governor-general; events unfolded as he urged.

sentences.zh: 各國相繼換約，交涉益劇，枋事者多依違。

translations.literal: As nations renewed treaties in succession, diplomacy grew still more intense, and many handling affairs wavered.
translations.idiomatic: As treaties were renewed in succession, diplomacy intensified and many handlers wavered.

sentences.zh: 家楣苦心經畫，凡議覲禮、遣使臣、護僑民，皆委曲歷久而後定。

translations.literal: Jiamei labored to plan matters; whether audience ritual, dispatch of envoys, or protection of overseas subjects, each was settled only after long and careful negotiation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamei labored over every issue—audience ritual, envoys, protection of subjects abroad—each settled only after prolonged negotiation.

sentences.zh: 洎日本闚台灣，海防亟，乃為策先謀足以製日者。

translations.literal: When Japan cast its eye on Taiwan and coastal defense grew urgent, he devised a strategy to seek first what could restrain Japan.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan eyed Taiwan and coastal defense grew urgent, he sought first a means to restrain Japan.

sentences.zh: 於是大學士文祥舉立海軍、造船艦、築砲台、制槍械、採煤鐵、招僑商，及用人、籌餉諸端，折衷眾說，屬草議上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Secretary Wen Xiang proposed establishing a navy, building warships, constructing batteries, manufacturing firearms, mining coal and iron, recruiting overseas merchants, and the matters of personnel and funds; weighing many opinions, he entrusted Jiamei to draft a memorial for submission.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wen Xiang proposed a navy, warships, batteries, firearms, coal and iron mines, overseas merchants, personnel, and funds; Jiamei was asked to draft the memorial synthesizing opinion.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，擢五品京堂。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director and was elevated to a fifth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director and then to a fifth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，除太僕寺少卿，典四川鄉試。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign he was appointed vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and presided over the Sichuan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangxu he became vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and presided over the Sichuan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 越二載，遷順天府府尹，兼總理各國事務大臣，遭憂去。

translations.literal: Two years later he was transferred to prefect of Shuntian and concurrently minister of the Zongli Yamen; he left office on mourning his father.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became prefect of Shuntian and Zongli Yamen minister, then left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，署左副都御史，直總署如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he acted as left vice censor-in-chief and continued his duties at the Yamen as before.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he acted as left vice censor-in-chief while continuing at the Yamen.

sentences.zh: 八年，再授順天府府尹。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again appointed prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 he was again appointed prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 時吏治日弛，家楣自初蒞即奏增經費，劾污吏，練捕盜營，親決獄訟，設通州、良鄉官車局、近畿教養義塾、善堂、留養局，增貢院號舍，擴金台書院，制孔廟祭器、樂器。

translations.literal: As governance daily slackened, from his first arrival Jiamei memorialized for increased funds, impeached corrupt officials, drilled anti-bandit camps, personally decided lawsuits, established official carriage offices at Tongzhou and Liangxiang, charity schools and halls in the capital region, relief bureaus, expanded examination cells, enlarged the Jintai Academy, and had Confucian temple vessels and musical instruments made.
translations.idiomatic: With governance slackening, from his first day he sought more funds, impeached corrupt officials, drilled constabulary camps, judged cases personally, founded carriage offices, charity schools, relief halls, expanded examination quarters and Jintai Academy, and commissioned temple vessels and instruments.

sentences.zh: 及再任，益有興革，郡中一切皆治辦。

translations.literal: On his second term he undertook still more reforms, and everything in the prefecture was put in order.
translations.idiomatic: On his second term reforms multiplied until the prefecture was fully in order.

sentences.zh: 九年，霪雨河溢，州邑籥菑，亟疏請帑，复募集銀百餘萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year prolonged rain caused rivers to overflow and districts and counties suffered disaster; he urgently memorialized for treasury funds and also raised more than a million taels in silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 floods devastated the region; he urgently sought treasury funds and raised over a million taels.

sentences.zh: 會關東大熟，勸募雜糧，亦獲數万石，卹飢困。

translations.literal: As Guandong had a great harvest, he urged collection of miscellaneous grain and obtained tens of thousands of shi as well, relieving hunger and distress.
translations.idiomatic: With a great harvest in Guandong he collected tens of thousands of shi of grain to relieve hunger.

sentences.zh: 明年春，大舉工賑，濬京南鳳河，京東北運河，武清、寶坻兩減河、宛平龐谷莊百二十村溝洫。

translations.literal: The next spring he launched large-scale work relief, dredging the Feng River south of the capital, the Grand Canal northeast of the capital, the reduction canals of Wuqing and Baodi, and the ditches of 120 villages at Pangguzhuang in Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring he launched work relief, dredging the Feng River, the northeast Grand Canal, Wuqing and Baodi reduction canals, and 120 village ditches at Pangguzhuang.

sentences.zh: 通州、涿州、霸州、保定堤壩決口，分助直、魯工賑皆鉅萬。

translations.literal: Dykes burst at Tongzhou, Zhuozhou, Bazhou, and Baoding; he assisted Zhili and Shandong relief works with sums of tens of thousands each.
translations.idiomatic: Dykes burst at Tongzhou, Zhuozhou, Bazhou, and Baoding; he gave tens of thousands each to Zhili and Shandong relief.

sentences.zh: 僉謂京畿救荒之政，為百年所未有云。

translations.literal: All agreed that famine relief in the capital region had not been seen in a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said capital-region famine relief had not been equaled in a century.

sentences.zh: 家楣方負時望，累兼署禮、戶、兵三部侍郎，上意駸鄉用。

translations.literal: Jiamei then bore high public hopes and was repeatedly appointed acting vice minister in the Boards of Rites, Revenue, and War; the emperor's intent was gradually to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamei enjoyed high repute and repeatedly acted as vice minister in Rites, Revenue, and War; the throne meant to promote him.

sentences.zh: 既而恭親王奕訢罷政，朝局一變。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Prince Gong Yixin was removed from power and the court situation changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Gong Yixin left power and the court situation shifted.

sentences.zh: 法越事起，朝士激昂多主戰。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict arose, court scholars were ardent and mostly favored war.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict arose, court scholars mostly favored war.

sentences.zh: 家楣以法彊盛，不可輕敵，乃自具疏，略謂：「法人肆擾海疆，台灣亟於戰禦，餉械阻絕。

translations.literal: Jiamei held that France was powerful and the enemy must not be lightly provoked; he drafted his own memorial, stating in summary: "The French are wantonly harassing the coasts; Taiwan urgently needs defense, and supplies and arms are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamei held France too strong to provoke lightly and memorialized in part: "The French harass the coasts; Taiwan needs defense urgently while pay and arms are cut off.

sentences.zh: 敵以兵船十數游弋海口，伺隙抵巇，各國且潛濟之。

translations.literal: The enemy cruises a dozen or so warships at the mouth of the sea, watching for openings to strike weak points, and other nations secretly aid them.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen enemy warships cruise the coast seeking openings, while other nations secretly aid them.

sentences.zh: 台灣雖勝，與內地隔。

translations.literal: Even if Taiwan is victorious, it is separated from the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Even victory in Taiwan leaves it cut off from the interior.

sentences.zh: 越南得手，得一地留一師，亦恐分兵致弱。

translations.literal: If Vietnam is taken, holding one place requires leaving one army, and dividing forces may lead to weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Each gain in Vietnam ties down an army and risks weakening forces elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 今調停之說，發之自彼，權之在我，不得不別具深謀，欲擒先縱。

translations.literal: Now mediation is proposed from their side, yet the decision rests with us; we must devise deeper strategy—to catch the prey one first lets it run.
translations.idiomatic: Mediation now comes from them, but the decision is ours; we need deeper strategy—to catch prey one first lets it run.

sentences.zh: 至中國實能自強，轉無戰之可言。

translations.literal: When China can truly strengthen itself, war will no longer be speakable.
translations.idiomatic: When China truly strengthens itself, war becomes unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 此大局之樞紐也。

translations.literal: This is the pivot of the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: This is the pivot of the larger situation.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，自知其言不協時，曰：「吾終不以附和誤國。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, knowing his words did not accord with the times, he said: "I will never join in flattery and harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: " When it went up, knowing his words were unpopular, he said: "I will never flatter the times and harm the state.

sentences.zh: 」給事中孔憲劾張廕桓洩漏機密，語連家楣及吳廷芬等，乃罷直總署，轉通政使。

translations.literal: " Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuang for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen and others; he was removed from duty at the Yamen and transferred to commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising Secretary Kong Xian impeached Zhang Yinhuang for leaking secrets, implicating Jiamei and Wu Tingfen; he left the Yamen for the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangxu 13.

sentences.zh: 順天士民感其遺惠，請建通州專祠，詔允之。

translations.literal: The scholars and people of Shuntian, grateful for his legacy of kindness, requested a dedicated shrine at Tongzhou, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian scholars and people, grateful for his legacy, won approval for a dedicated shrine at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 周德潤，字生霖，廣西臨桂人。

translations.literal: Zhou Derun, style name Shenglin, was a native of Lingui in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Derun, style Shenglin, came from Lingui in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 同治元年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he took his jinshi, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷司業，歷侍讀學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of studies, served in succession as reader-in-waiting, and was appointed recorder of the emperor's daily activities.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of studies, reader-in-waiting, and recorder of the emperor's daily activities.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，除少詹事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Guangxu reign he was appointed junior vice director of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8 he was appointed junior vice director of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 星變陳言，上修理政刑六事。

translations.literal: On an irregularity in the heavens he memorialized, submitting six matters for repairing governance and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On a celestial anomaly he memorialized six measures to repair governance and punishment.

sentences.zh: 再遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十年，大學士左宗棠稱疾請解職，德潤力言：「宗棠不宜去位，請旨責其引退之非，示以致身之義。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang claimed illness and requested to resign office; Derun strongly argued: "Zongtang should not leave his post; I request an edict reproving his error in seeking retirement and showing the meaning of giving one's person to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang sought to resign on illness; Derun argued: "Zongtang must not leave office; I ask an edict reproving his retirement and teaching devotion to the state.

sentences.zh: 」稱旨。

translations.literal: " This accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，言路發攄，德潤先後劾巡撫李文敏、倪文蔚不職狀，有直聲。

translations.literal: At that time the remonstrance channels were active; Derun successively impeached Governors Li Wenmin and Ni Wenwei for dereliction of duty and gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance flourished; Derun impeached Governors Li Wenmin and Ni Wenwei for neglect and gained a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 法越構兵，倡救越議，數請力保籓封，速定戰計，條列急務十端，可危者八，不可和者五，宜用兵者七。

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam went to war he advocated saving Vietnam, repeatedly requesting firm protection of the tributary state, swift settlement of war plans, listing ten urgent matters, eight points of danger, five reasons peace was impossible, and seven cases where force should be used.
translations.idiomatic: When France and Vietnam fought he urged saving Vietnam, repeatedly demanding protection of the tributary, swift war plans, ten urgent matters, eight dangers, five reasons peace was impossible, and seven cases for force.

sentences.zh: 又以防務不可歲月計，復請亟籌強邊積穀，以老敵師、操勝算。

translations.literal: He also held that coastal defense could not be planned by the month and again requested urgent accumulation of grain on strong frontiers to wear down the enemy and secure victory.
translations.idiomatic: He also said coastal defense could not wait months and urged grain stockpiles on the frontiers to wear down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 疏凡十餘上，上數召見，嘉其諳邊情。

translations.literal: His memorials totaled more than ten; the emperor repeatedly summoned him and praised his knowledge of frontier conditions.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten memorials; the emperor repeatedly summoned him and praised his frontier knowledge.

sentences.zh: 命行走總理各國事務衙門，兩次請敕廷臣集議。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen and twice requested that the court order ministers to meet in conference.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to the Zongli Yamen and twice asked for ministerial conferences.

sentences.zh: 未幾，和議起，法人勒退兵，益索償費。

translations.literal: Before long peace talks began; the French demanded withdrawal of troops and further sought indemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon peace talks began; France demanded troop withdrawal and further indemnity.

sentences.zh: 議者欲與之，德潤持不可，謂：「苟傷國體，即一介不可與。

translations.literal: Those in council wished to grant it; Derun held this unacceptable, saying: "If national dignity is harmed, not even a single cash may be given.
translations.idiomatic: Councilors wished to pay; Derun refused, saying: "If national dignity is harmed, not one cash may be given.

sentences.zh: 請定志毋退縮。

translations.literal: I request that resolve be fixed and no retreat made.
translations.idiomatic: Fix resolve and do not retreat.

sentences.zh: 」已，議敘事棘，德潤獨具疏，略言：「籓封可棄，猶謂非域中也。

translations.literal: " Later, as negotiations grew difficult, Derun submitted a memorial alone, stating in summary: "The tributary state may be abandoned, yet one may still say it is not within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " As negotiations hardened, Derun memorialized alone: "The tributary may be abandoned, yet one may still say it is not the heartland.

sentences.zh: 邊界可分，猶謂非腹地也。

translations.literal: Boundaries may be divided, yet one may still say it is not the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Borders may be divided, yet one may still say it is not the interior.

sentences.zh: 商可通，兵可撤，猶謂守約非背約也。

translations.literal: Trade may be opened and troops withdrawn, yet one may still say this keeps the treaty and does not break it.
translations.idiomatic: Trade may open and troops withdraw, yet one may still call this keeping treaty faith.

sentences.zh: 五條外橫生枝節，若猶遷就，其何能國？

translations.literal: Beyond the five articles new branches arise; if we still yield, how can the state endure?
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the five articles new demands sprout; further yielding would destroy the state.

sentences.zh: 請嚴拒之。

translations.literal: I request strict rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Reject them strictly.

sentences.zh: 」並陳和戰機宜甚悉。

translations.literal: " He also set forth the opportunities of peace and war in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He also detailed peace-and-war opportunities at length.

sentences.zh: 上以單銜入告，乖和衷誼，罷直總署。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he reported alone and violated the spirit of harmony, removed him from duty at the Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting alone and violating harmonious counsel, he was removed from the Yamen.

sentences.zh: 及明詔與法宣戰，德潤遵旨覆陳台、越戰計，力駁德璀琳、盛宣懷所擬和約，條列救台复越六策，力主先戰後和。

translations.literal: When an explicit edict declared war on France, Derun followed instructions and memorialized again on Taiwan and Vietnam war plans, forcefully refuting the draft treaties of Detring and Sheng Xuanhuai, listing six measures to save Taiwan and recover Vietnam, and strongly advocating war before peace.
translations.idiomatic: When war on France was declared, Derun followed orders, refuted Detring and Sheng Xuanhuai's draft treaties, listed six measures to save Taiwan and recover Vietnam, and urged war before peace.

sentences.zh: 复上安徽釐稅、梧州關稅積弊狀，先後命大臣廉得實，設法整飭之，歲課贏數十萬。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on longstanding abuses in Anhui transit duties and Wuzhou customs; the court repeatedly ordered ministers to investigate and verify, instituted reforms, and annual revenue increased by several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed abuses in Anhui transit duties and Wuzhou customs; investigations led to reforms yielding hundreds of thousands more in annual revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，和議將成，德潤臚舉八事進，曰：習勤苦；

translations.literal: The following year, as peace was about to be concluded, Derun set forth eight matters in full, namely: practice diligence and hardship;
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as peace neared, Derun listed eight measures: practice diligence;

sentences.zh: 責疆吏；

translations.literal: hold frontier officials accountable;
translations.idiomatic: hold frontier officials accountable;

sentences.zh: 清內宄；

translations.literal: clear internal malfeasance;
translations.idiomatic: purge internal malfeasance;

sentences.zh: 募銳卒；

translations.literal: recruit elite troops;
translations.idiomatic: recruit elite troops;

sentences.zh: 杜中飽；

translations.literal: stop middlemen from profiteering;
translations.idiomatic: stop middlemen from profiteering;

sentences.zh: 會辦北洋大臣宜分駐奉天海口，南北宜聯一氣；

translations.literal: the co-managing minister for the Northern Seas should divide his station between Fengtian and the sea mouth, and north and south should act as one;
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Seas co-minister should station separately at Fengtian and the coast, and north and south should unite;

sentences.zh: 滇、粵宜籌善後；

translations.literal: Yunnan and Guangdong should plan for aftermath;
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Guangdong need postwar planning;

sentences.zh: 雲南宜設機器局。

translations.literal: Yunnan should establish a machine works.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan should establish a machine works.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時法使浦理燮等赴越，朝命德潤詣滇治界務。

translations.literal: At that time the French envoy Poulois and others went to Vietnam; the court ordered Derun to proceed to Yunnan to handle boundary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: French envoys went to Vietnam; the court sent Derun to Yunnan on boundaries.

sentences.zh: 德潤率道員葉廷眷等出關，勘都霙南丹古林箐，緣南溪河至河口保勝蠻耗。

translations.literal: Derun led Circuit Intendant Ye Tingjuan and others beyond the pass, surveyed Duying, Nandan, Gulin Gorge, followed the Nanxi River to Hekou, Baosheng, and Manhao.
translations.idiomatic: Derun led Ye Tingjuan beyond the pass, surveyed Duying, Nandan, Gulin Gorge, and followed the Nanxi to Hekou and Baosheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與法使狄隆等論界線，以緣邊二千餘裡，議分五段，執志乘與爭，更正沒入越地三十餘裡，險要地四十里，復大賭咒河外苗塘子諸地數百里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he negotiated boundary lines with the French envoy Detring and others; along more than two thousand li of border they divided discussion into five sections, argued from local gazetteers, corrected more than thirty li of land wrongly absorbed into Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and recovered several hundred li beyond Duzhou including Miaotangzi and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12 he negotiated boundaries with Detring along two thousand li, divided work into five sections, cited gazetteers, recovered thirty li wrongly lost to Vietnam, forty li of strategic ground, and hundreds of li beyond Duzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾歲還，除刑部侍郎，督順天學政。

translations.literal: A year later he returned and was appointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments and supervised education in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned, became vice minister of Punishments, and supervised Shuntian education.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，予優恤。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died and was granted generous posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 18 he died with generous posthumous favors.

sentences.zh: 胡燏棻，字芸楣，安徽泗州人，本籍浙江蕭山。

translations.literal: Hu Yufen, style name Yunmei, was a native of Sizhou in Anhui, with original household registration in Xiaoshan, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yufen, style Yunmei, was registered in Sizhou, Anhui, with ancestral home in Xiaoshan, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Tongzhi reign he passed the metropolitan examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 he took his jinshi and entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 散館，改知廣西靈川縣，未上，納貲為道員，銓直隸。

translations.literal: After leaving the Hanlin he was transferred to magistrate of Lingchuan in Guangxi; before taking up the post he purchased office as a circuit intendant and was assigned to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Hanlin, he was named magistrate of Lingchuan but bought office as a circuit intendant in Zhili instead.

sentences.zh: 總督李鴻章俾筦北洋軍糈，補天津道。

translations.literal: Governor-General Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang military provisions and he was appointed prefect of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang put him in charge of Beiyang provisions and appointed him Tianjin prefect.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，鴻章將出閱海軍，有巨猾覬為變，流言胥動。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Guangxu reign Li Hongzhang was about to review the navy; a major villain plotted disorder and rumors stirred everyone.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 14 Li Hongzhang was to review the navy; a major plotter stirred rumors of revolt.

sentences.zh: 各國領事詰鴻章，鴻章以其事屬燏棻，越三月捕治之，民乃定。

translations.literal: Foreign consuls questioned Li Hongzhang, who entrusted the matter to Yufen; within three months the culprit was captured and punished, and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Consuls questioned Li Hongzhang, who entrusted the case to Yufen; within three months the plotter was caught and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 海舟應徭自奉天運米豆輸天津，充戶長者，歲出金三萬，往往破家。

translations.literal: Sea vessels performing corvée duty transported grain and beans from Fengtian to Tianjin; those serving as household heads paid thirty thousand cash yearly and often were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée grain ships from Fengtian to Tianjin made household heads pay thirty thousand cash yearly, often ruining families.

sentences.zh: 燏棻廉得狀，上鴻章奏罷之。

translations.literal: Yufen investigated and reported the facts to Li Hongzhang, who memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yufen investigated and Li Hongzhang memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大水，民數万止城上。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year great floods struck and tens of thousands of people took refuge on the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 16 floods drove tens of thousands onto the city walls.

sentences.zh: 燏棻擴北倉、西沽粥廠徙居之。

translations.literal: Yufen expanded the North Granary and the Xigu porridge kitchens to relocate them.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the North Granary and Xigu soup kitchens to house them.

sentences.zh: 鴻章用其言，募集銀三百數十萬，复督塞南北運河諸溢流凡八十餘處，民猶及種麥。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang adopted his plan, raised more than three million taels in silver, and again supervised blocking more than eighty overflow points on the north and south Grand Canal so the people could still plant wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang adopted his plan, raised over three million taels, and blocked eighty canal overflows so farmers could still plant wheat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷廣西按察使，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Guangxi and granted first-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 17 he became Guangxi judicial commissioner with first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 逾歲到官，多所平反。

translations.literal: More than a year after arriving he reversed many wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: After arriving he reversed many wrongful verdicts.

sentences.zh: 兩權布政使，建遜業堂教士，下臨桂知縣督諸囚習藝。

translations.literal: He twice acted as financial commissioner, built the Xunye Hall to teach scholars, and ordered the Lin'gui magistrate to supervise prisoners in crafts.
translations.idiomatic: He twice acted as financial commissioner, founded the Xunye Hall, and had Lin'gui magistrate supervise prisoner crafts.

sentences.zh: 二十年，入覲，會中東事起，命治糈台。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he went to court audience; as conflict in the Middle East arose he was ordered to manage the provisions bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he attended court; with war in the Middle East he managed the provisions bureau.

sentences.zh: 師挫，鴻章東渡行成。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated Li Hongzhang crossed to Japan to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat Li Hongzhang went to Japan for peace.

sentences.zh: 諸軍西入關，燏棻疏請資遣之。

translations.literal: As armies entered the pass westward, Yufen memorialized requesting funds for their discharge.
translations.idiomatic: As armies entered the pass, Yufen memorialized funds to discharge them.

sentences.zh: 蔣希夷軍幾潰，燏棻單騎宣諭，卒解遣，無敢譁者。

translations.literal: Jiang Xiyi's army nearly mutinied; Yufen went alone on horseback to proclaim the edict, and the troops were finally dismissed without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiyi's army nearly mutinied; Yufen rode alone to proclaim the edict and dismissed them without riot.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恫喪師，知募兵不足恃，命燏棻主練兵，成十營，頓小站，號定武軍。

translations.literal: The court, alarmed at losing troops, knew recruited soldiers were unreliable and ordered Yufen to train troops; ten battalions were formed, stationed at Xiaozhan, and called the Dingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed at defeat, the court knew mercenaries unreliable and had Yufen train ten battalions at Xiaozhan as the Dingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 小站練兵自此始。

translations.literal: Training troops at Xiaozhan began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhan troop training began here.

sentences.zh: 燏棻上疏言變法自強，條列十事：曰開鐵路，自漢口至京為幹路，其分支南自光山、固始出六安，自應城、京山、安陸出荊門、當陽；

translations.literal: Yufen memorialized on reform and self-strengthening, listing ten matters: open railways, with a trunk line from Hankou to the capital and branches south from Guangshan and Gushi through Lu'an, and from Yingcheng, Jingshan, and Anlu through Jingmen and Dangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yufen memorialized ten reforms: railways with a Hankou-Beijing trunk and branches south via Guangshan-Gushi-Lu'an and Yingcheng-Jingshan-Anlu-Jingmen-Dangyang;

sentences.zh: 西自懷慶出軹關迳蒲、解達關隴；

translations.literal: west from Huaiqing through Jiguan Pass by way of Pu and Jie to reach Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: west from Huaiqing through Jiguan Pass to Guanzhong;

sentences.zh: 東自開封、歸德過宿、泗抵清江。

translations.literal: east from Kaifeng and Guide through Su and Si to reach Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: east from Kaifeng and Guide through Su and Si to Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 曰造鈔幣、銀幣，毋使各國壟市利。

translations.literal: mint paper and silver currency so foreign nations cannot monopolize market profit.
translations.idiomatic: On minting paper and silver currency to stop foreign monopoly of profit.

sentences.zh: 曰制機器，國家用槍砲船械，令民廠自造，可塞漏卮。

translations.literal: manufacture machines; the state uses firearms, cannon, ships, and implements—let civilian factories make them and the leak in the treasury can be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On manufacturing machines so state arms and ships can be made domestically, stopping fiscal leakage.

sentences.zh: 曰開礦產，築路需煤鐵，鑄幣需金銀銅，制機器需五金，擇良吏主其事。

translations.literal: open mineral resources; building roads needs coal and iron, minting needs gold, silver, and copper, machines need metals—select good officials to manage the work.
translations.idiomatic: On opening mines: roads need coal and iron, coinage needs metals, machines need alloys—appoint capable officials.

sentences.zh: 曰折南漕，官祿軍糈並易以銀，仍就津市米儲通州，備緩急。

translations.literal: commute Southern Transport grain; official salaries and military rations all exchanged for silver, while grain from Tianjin markets is stored at Tongzhou for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: On commuting Southern Transport to silver pay while storing Tianjin grain at Tongzhou for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 曰減兵額，汰老弱，簡精壯，化無用為有用。

translations.literal: reduce troop quotas, eliminate the old and weak, select the elite and strong, turning the useless into the useful.
