translations.idiomatic: On cutting troop quotas, eliminating weak soldiers, and making the remainder useful.

sentences.zh: 曰創郵政，取其貲佐度支，驛站、提塘皆可廢。

translations.literal: create a postal service, using its revenue to assist state expenditure; courier stations and dispatch offices may all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On creating postal service revenue for the treasury and abolishing courier stations.

sentences.zh: 曰練陸軍，將知學問，械求​​畫一，兵取良家，厚將領月糈，嚴戒侵蝕。

translations.literal: train the land army; generals must know learning, weapons must be uniform, soldiers taken from good families, officers' monthly pay increased, and corruption strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On training the army with educated generals, uniform weapons, respectable recruits, better pay, and no corruption.

sentences.zh: 曰整海軍，軍置帥，總領緣海七省，隸中樞，不受疆吏節度。

translations.literal: organize the navy; place a commander over the seven coastal provinces, subordinate to the center and not to provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: On organizing a navy commander over seven coastal provinces, answerable to the center not governors.

sentences.zh: 曰設學堂，農、商、工、礦、醫有顓家，水師、陸軍、女子、盲啞有教法，朝廷為定制，甄而用之。

translations.literal: establish schools; agriculture, commerce, industry, mining, and medicine each have specialists; naval, army, women's, and blind-deaf-mute instruction each has methods—the court sets standards and selects graduates for use.
translations.idiomatic: On establishing specialized schools for agriculture, commerce, industry, mining, medicine, navy, army, women, and disabled instruction under court standards.

sentences.zh: 又言停武科，練旗兵，器械、營製、餉章並從西式。

translations.literal: He also said to abolish the military examination, train Banner troops, and make weapons, camp organization, and pay regulations all follow Western forms.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged abolishing military exams, training Banner troops, and westernizing arms, camps, and pay.

sentences.zh: 次第皆採用。

translations.literal: These were adopted in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: These were adopted in turn.

sentences.zh: 是歲定議造鐵路，自盧​​溝至津，命燏棻充督辦。

translations.literal: That year it was decided to build a railway from Lugou Bridge to Tianjin, and Yufen was appointed superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: That year a Lugou Bridge-Tianjin railway was approved with Yufen as superintendent.

sentences.zh: 尋授順天府府尹，疏請展京西支路，首盧溝訖門頭溝，便煤運。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed prefect of Shuntian and memorialized to extend branch lines west of the capital, first from Lugou Bridge to Mentougou to facilitate coal transport.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Shuntian prefect and memorialized a western branch from Lugou Bridge to Mentougou for coal.

sentences.zh: 已，充總理各國事務大臣，時董福祥軍駐南苑，斫傷鐵路西國工程師，各公使訴於朝，請罷董軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as minister of the Zongli Yamen; at that time Dong Fuxiang's army was stationed at the Southern Hunting Park and wounded a Western engineer on the railway; the envoys appealed to the court to dismiss Dong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Later at the Zongli Yamen, Dong Fuxiang's troops at the Southern Hunting Park wounded a foreign railway engineer; envoys demanded their removal.

sentences.zh: 燏棻力爭，始留駐近畿，然卒以此罷直總署。

translations.literal: Yufen argued forcefully and they were finally kept near the capital, yet he was dismissed from duty at the Yamen for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yufen argued they should stay near the capital; he kept them but lost his Yamen post.

sentences.zh: 燏棻夙以談洋務著稱。

translations.literal: Yufen had long been renowned for discussing foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yufen was long known for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 次年，拳匪入京，指為通敵，欲殺之，逸而免。

translations.literal: The following year Boxers entered the capital, denounced him as communicating with the enemy, and sought to kill him, but he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Boxers entered Beijing, called him a traitor, and tried to kill him; he escaped.

sentences.zh: 膺會辦關內外鐵路之命，路為聯軍佔，歲餘始與英使訂約接收，復歸於我。

translations.literal: He received appointment to co-manage railways inside and outside the pass; the railways were occupied by the allied armies and only after more than a year did he conclude a treaty with the British envoy to receive them back.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed to co-manage railways, he recovered them from allied occupation only after a year of negotiation with Britain.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部右侍郎，三十二年，轉禮部，尋轉郵傳部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Punishments; in the thirty-second year to the Board of Rites, and soon to the Ministry of Posts.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of Punishments, then in Guangxu 32 Rites, then Posts.

sentences.zh: 卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous favors followed statute.
translations.idiomatic: He died with statutory posthumous favors.

sentences.zh: 予天津建祠。

translations.literal: A shrine was granted at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was granted in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 張廕桓，字樵野，廣東南海人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yinhuang, style name Qiaoye, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yinhuang, style Qiaoye, came from Nanhai in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 性通侻。

translations.literal: By nature he was versatile and unconventional.
translations.idiomatic: He was versatile and unconventional by nature.

sentences.zh: 納貲為知縣，銓山東。

translations.literal: He purchased office as a magistrate and was assigned to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as a magistrate in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫閻敬銘、丁寶楨先後器異之，數薦至道員，光緒二年，權登萊青道。

translations.literal: Governors Yan Jingming and Ding Baozhen both valued him highly and repeatedly recommended him to circuit intendant; in the second year of the Guangxu reign he acted as intendant of Deng-Lai-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Yan Jingming and Ding Baozhen valued him and raised him to circuit intendant; in Guangxu 2 he acted Deng-Lai-Qing intendant.

sentences.zh: 時英國請闢煙台租界，議倡馬頭捐以斂厚貲，廕桓持不可。

translations.literal: At that time Britain requested a concession at Yantai; some proposed a wharf levy to raise large funds, but Yinhuang held this unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain sought a Yantai concession, some proposed a wharf levy; Yinhuang refused.

sentences.zh: 又義塚一區為人盜售，有司已鈐契矣；

translations.literal: There was also a charitable burial ground sold by thieves, and the authorities had already sealed the deed;
translations.idiomatic: A charitable burial ground was sold by thieves and officials had already sealed the deed;

sentences.zh: 復與力爭，卒返其地。

translations.literal: he again argued forcefully and in the end the land was returned.
translations.idiomatic: he argued forcefully and recovered the land.

sentences.zh: 七年，授安徽徽寧池太廣道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed intendant of Huining-Chi-Tai-Guang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7 he became Huining-Chi-Tai-Guang intendant.

sentences.zh: 抉蕪湖關痼弊，稅驟進。

translations.literal: He exposed chronic abuses at Wuhu customs and tax revenue surged.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Wuhu customs abuses and revenue surged.

sentences.zh: 會久霪雨，江流衍溢，州邑籥菑，出俸錢賑之。

translations.literal: As prolonged rain caused rivers to overflow and districts suffered disaster, he spent his salary on relief.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck; he spent his salary on relief.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徵還，賞三品京堂，命直總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he was granted third-rank capital official and ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he received third-rank capital rank and entered the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 十年，除太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 he became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 廕桓精敏，號知外務。

translations.literal: Yinhuang was keen and sharp and was known for understanding foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yinhuang was sharp and known for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 驟躋巍官，務攬權，為同列所忌。

translations.literal: He rose rapidly to high office, strove to gather power, and was resented by colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: He rose fast, grasped power, and colleagues resented him.

sentences.zh: 給事中孔憲摭其致蘇松太道邵友濂私函為洩朝旨，劾之，詔出總署。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Kong Xian seized his private letter to Su-Song-Tai Circuit Intendant Shao Youlian as leaking court intent and impeached him; an edict removed him from the Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xian impeached him for leaking court intent via a letter to Shao Youlian; an edict removed him from the Yamen.

sentences.zh: 又以語連同官，並罷周家楣等，朝列益銜之。

translations.literal: Because his words implicated colleagues, Zhou Jiamei and others were dismissed as well, and the court increasingly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His words implicated Zhou Jiamei and others, who were dismissed too, deepening court resentment.

sentences.zh: 左遷直隸大順廣道。

translations.literal: He was demoted to intendant of Da-Shun-Guang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Da-Shun-Guang intendant in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命充出使美日秘三國大臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed envoy to the United States, Japan, and Peru.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11 he was appointed envoy to the United States, Japan, and Peru.

sentences.zh: 逾歲赴美，舟抵金山，稅司黑假索觀國書，廕桓謂非關吏所得預，峻拒之。

translations.literal: The following year he went to America; when his ship reached Jinshan the customs officer Black demanded to see the imperial credentials; Yinhuang said this was not within a customs officer's purview and refused sternly.
translations.idiomatic: Going to America, at Jinshan customs officer Black demanded credentials; Yinhuang refused sternly.

sentences.zh: 電詰美外部，黑假踧踖慚謝。

translations.literal: He telegraphed the American foreign ministry; Black became embarrassed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He telegraphed the U.S. State Department; Black apologized.

sentences.zh: 至伊士頓，地近洛士丙冷，華民簞食相迎，初，華民之傭其地也，為美工燔殺，數至二百餘人。

translations.literal: At Easton, near Los Angeles, Chinese residents welcomed him with simple meals; earlier Chinese laborers hired in that region had been killed by Americans in fires, numbering more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Easton near Los Angeles, Chinese welcomed him; earlier more than two hundred Chinese laborers had been killed there.

sentences.zh: 前使鄭藻如索償所毀財產，久不得直，至是皆待命廕桓。

translations.literal: Former envoy Zheng Zaoru had sought compensation for destroyed property but long received no satisfaction; now all awaited Yinhuang's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Zheng Zaoru had sought compensation in vain; all now awaited Yinhuang.

sentences.zh: 廕桓既達美都，即與其外部辨論，凡償墨西哥銀十四萬七千有奇。

translations.literal: Once Yinhuang reached the American capital he argued with their foreign ministry and obtained Mexican silver totaling 147,000-odd in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: In Washington he obtained 147,000-odd in Mexican silver compensation.

sentences.zh: 金山華民故好械鬥，嘗為文諷諭之。

translations.literal: Chinese at Jinshan were fond of armed fights; he once wrote an essay admonishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshan Chinese often fought; he wrote to admonish them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，美設苛例，欲禁遏華工。

translations.literal: Before long America set harsh regulations seeking to restrict Chinese laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon America set harsh rules against Chinese laborers.

sentences.zh: 廕桓曰：「與其係命它族，毋寧靳勿與通也。

translations.literal: Yinhuang said: "Rather than leave their lives in other nations' hands, better to forbid passage altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Yinhuang said: "Better forbid emigration than leave lives to others.

sentences.zh: 」於是倡自禁華工議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he initiated a proposal for China itself to ban Chinese laborers.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed China ban Chinese labor emigration.

sentences.zh: 繼乃徇眾請，不果行。

translations.literal: Later he yielded to public request and the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Later he yielded to public pressure and dropped it.

sentences.zh: 其它烏盧公司槐花園、澳路非奴、姑力、阿路美、的欽巴新蕾諸案，亦多所斡旋。

translations.literal: Other cases such as Uluc, Huaihuayuan, Aolufei, Guli, Alumei, and Deqin Baxinlei were also much mediated by him.
translations.idiomatic: He also mediated cases at Uluc, Huaihuayuan, Aolufei, and other places.

sentences.zh: 又與日廷爭論小呂宋設官事，卒如所議。

translations.literal: He also argued with Japan over establishing officials in little Luzon, and in the end matters proceeded as he proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with Japan over officials in little Luzon and won his terms.

sentences.zh: 是歲，除太常寺卿，轉通政司副使。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became minister of Imperial Sacrifices, then vice transmission commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，奏設古巴學堂，並籌建金山學堂、醫院。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized to establish a school in Cuba and planned schools and hospitals at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 he memorialized a Cuba school and planned Jinshan schools and hospitals.

sentences.zh: 後三年還國，仍直總署。

translations.literal: Three years later he returned and again served in the Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he returned to the Yamen.

sentences.zh: 歷遷戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to left vice minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日議和，命偕友濂為全權大臣，東渡，日人弗納。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as China and Japan negotiated peace, he was ordered together with Youlian to serve as plenipotentiary ministers and cross to Japan, but the Japanese would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he and Youlian were plenipotentiaries to Japan, but Japan refused them.

sentences.zh: 次年，復命與日使林董賡議商約，廕桓力爭優待利益、徵收稅則二事，成通商行船二十九款，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: The following year he was again ordered with Japanese envoy Hayashi to negotiate commercial treaties; Yinhuang strongly contested preferential benefits and tax rates, completing twenty-nine articles on commerce and shipping, detailed in the Treaties section.
translations.idiomatic: Next year with envoy Hayashi he negotiated twenty-nine commercial articles on benefits and taxes, detailed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，奉使賀英，上以其領度支熟知外情，命就彼國兼議加稅，堅拒免釐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, sent to congratulate Britain, because he headed revenue and knew foreign conditions he was ordered while there also to negotiate increased taxation; he firmly refused exemption from transit dues.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 23, sent to congratulate Britain, he was also to negotiate taxes and refused likin exemption.

sentences.zh: 廕桓歷英、美、法、德、俄而還，條具聞見，累疏以陳。

translations.literal: Yinhuang traveled through Britain, America, France, Germany, and Russia and returned, setting forth what he had seen and heard in successive memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Britain, America, France, Germany, and Russia and memorialized his observations.

sentences.zh: 大恉謂宜屏外援，籌固圉，為箴膏起廢策。

translations.literal: His great theme was that foreign aid should be set aside, defenses strengthened, and policies offered like medicine for a wasting illness to revive the state.
translations.idiomatic: He urged rejecting foreign dependence, strengthening defenses, and revival policies like medicine for a wasting state.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，京師設礦務鐵路總局，被命主其事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the capital established a Mining and Railway Bureau and he was appointed to head it.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 he headed the capital Mining and Railway Bureau.

sentences.zh: 數言修內政以戢民志，治團練以裕兵力，敕並依行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly said to repair internal governance to calm popular will and organize militia to augment military strength; edicts ordered all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He urged internal reform and militia training; edicts ordered both carried out.

sentences.zh: 先是變法議起，主事康有為與往還甚密。

translations.literal: Earlier, when reform proposals arose, Clerk Kang Youwei had been in very close contact with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when reform arose, Clerk Kang Youwei was very close to him.

sentences.zh: 有為獲譴，遂褫廕桓職，謫戍新疆。

translations.literal: Youwei was punished; Yinhuang was then stripped of office and banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei was punished; Yinhuang was stripped of office and banished to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 越二年，拳亂作，用事者矯詔僇異己，廕桓論斬戍所。

translations.literal: Two years later the Boxer disorder erupted; those in power forged edicts to destroy opponents, and Yinhuang was sentenced to execution at the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Boxers rose; power-holders forged edicts against foes and sentenced Yinhuang to death in banishment.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復故官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 27 he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光緒朝部院大臣多負物望，其兼直總署者，時方重交涉，權比樞廷。

translations.literal: The commentators say: In the Guangxu reign many ministers of boards and courts bore public esteem; those who concurrently served in the Yamen, as foreign relations were then heavily weighted, held power comparable to the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: In Guangxu many ministers were esteemed; Yamen ministers handling foreign affairs held power like Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 樹銘、允升通經明律，家楣、德潤議約論戰，燏棻熟時務，廕桓諳外交，皆各有建白，一時理亂，實隱系之。

translations.literal: Shuming and Yunsheng mastered classics and law; Jiamei and Derun debated treaties and war; Yufen knew current affairs; Yinhuang understood diplomacy—each offered proposals, and the order and disorder of the age truly hinged on them in hidden ways.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming and Yunsheng mastered classics and law; Jiamei and Derun debated treaties and war; Yufen knew current affairs; Yinhuang knew diplomacy—each advised, and the age's fate hinged on them.

sentences.zh: 鳴鑾以妄言罷斥，論者疑非其罪。

translations.literal: Mingluan was dismissed for reckless speech; critics doubted it was his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Mingluan was dismissed for reckless speech; critics doubted the charge.

sentences.zh: 延煦爭謁陵拜跪，劾朝賀亂班，侃侃尤無愧禮臣雲。

translations.literal: Yanxu contested bowing and kneeling at the tomb visit and impeached disorder in congratulatory ranks—among ritual officials he was especially blameless, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxu fought for tomb ritual and impeached disorder at court congratulations—among ritualists he was especially blameless, it is said.
